Q: do you have any tips for a speaking presentation i have to do in 8 days in front of my whole school that im woefully unprepared for pls help

item.title: the US state i live in has exactly 2 area codes, and they both play the exact same tones when you dial them from a touch-tone phone. and i think that's pretty fuckin cool.
item.description:
7.1.26 2:45 pm
Q: the US state i live in has exactly 2 area codes, and they both play the exact same tones when you dial them from a touch-tone phone. and i think that's pretty fuckin cool.
A: it's only half true, but still cool. all the tones on a touch tone phone are different, they have to be, otherwise the phone system wouldnt be able to tell the numbers apart. but what you probably are hearing is just one of the two tones in each number. each number has 2 tones together, and if i remember correctly all the numbers in a column have one of the tones the same, and all the numbers in a row have the other tone the same. so if you have 2 area codes that sound the same to you, that means they either hit the exact exact same rows or the exact same columns. looking at this map, i think the only state i see where this works is west virginia, which has only two area codes and they both go 'last column, middle column, first column'. so you will hear the same melody in both codes, while also hearing a different melody underneath that. as if you have 2 singers, one singer is singing the same melody twice, but the backup singer does it different the second time. to isolate the difference, and i will assume for a moment that this is west virginia (304/681) type 36363636 to hear the difference between those two. then type 80808080 to hear the difference between those two, and then type 41414141 to hear the difference between those two. with these toggles you will hear one of the tones changing while the other stays the same. then you will probably be start to hear the difference better between the two area codes

item.title: how does anyone ever get a very specific noise? im talking like sound effects. foley artists are a mystery to me.
item.description:
7.1.26 11:34 pm
Q: how does anyone ever get a very specific noise? im talking like sound effects. foley artists are a mystery to me.
A: really the trick with foley is, you'd be surprised what you can get away with. if you put something at the right time, you can almost make anything out of anything. Hopefully you will find yourself on a mega time- or budget-constraint sometime, because that's when you will actually realize "oh crap, i absolutely didnt need to find a [some specific object] i literally just did it with my shirt." What you wanna do is get the headphones on, and, actually, if you just do things with your hands directly in front of the mic, you can almost get all the sounds you ever need. Furthermore, i would argue that you SHOULD deliberately cut creative corners like this, because as of now, if you actually seek out the most 'realistic' thing, your reward will only be that the audience will just assume you could have used ai for it. or stock, or whatever. so you get hella bonus points for humble charm, starting now. but, as i said, you'd be shocked at how effective you can be with things that are totally not actually the thing. if you get the timing and length right, the imagination will do the rest and it will be arguably much stronger than if you had gone out of your way to find an actual [actual thing in the scene]

Q: how do you sync your animations to your music (changing onscreen text with the lyrics, etc) so well? it's something i've always struggled with in my own editing but i'm sure it's bc of my method or my software
A: ultimately you'll need to have time navigation controls you're comfortable with (frame by frame, then something a little larger, then something a little larger) and then, crucially, you'll need to turn on audio-scrubbing mode. which means it plays you a tiny fraction of the audio at whatever frame you're at. so you can hear where you are. usually it takes some fooling around in the preferences and settings to get your techniques down, but you need frame by frame navigation and you need to hear the scrub. this is a normal feature for any software. possibly also may help to have drumming experience, because that just gives you a keen understanding of time in general

This is essentially the exact same game i'm playing here (in many cases i am taking these song choices straight from the 'Real Book' which is possibly the most well-known fakebook of my lifetime, in other cases i'm just doing them from memory). And the other reason why it is a fake ensemble is because it's actually just me. Another resason you might call it fake is because in a 'jazz ensemble' you might expect to have an acoustic horn instrument (such as saxophone or trumpet) playing the lead, and in this case i'm using an obnoxious synth instead. so that's 3 different reasons to invoke the word 'fake'

item.title: why do so many people insist on using choruses? i feel like verses do just fine on their own
item.description:
7.18.26 12:04 am
Q: why do so many people insist on using choruses? i feel like verses do just fine on their own
A: i think more people think there are more choruses than there actually are choruses. i think you might be fond of a very standard style which used to be used constantly and is STILL used quite a lot (i use it all the time), known as "AABA". you might say it goes 'verse, verse, B section, verse'. and the verse usually has the title in it. So is the verse actually the chorus? maybe, even though it has different lyrics every time and it starts the song. so then is the B section the chorus? not really, if anything it sounds more like a bridge. it's AABA. then usually after the AABA you'll have an instrumental solo over maybe one A, then the lyrics jump back in for a second B, then to one more A with a tag at the end where you repeat the last line or something like that. Additionally, besides AABA, there are also many other kinds of song forms which are very popular and which dont really have a 'chorus'. as i said, it's more often that people 'think' all songs have choruses than they actually do
